_meta.note: Bring HeartBeat to OpenCode (SST opencode 0.15.3, verified installed) — our THIRD MCP-client host after Codex and Claude Code. Investigation findings: (A) `opencode run --format json` is the headless Stage-B mode (like `claude -p`/`codex exec`); model via -m provider/model; the autonomy gotcha (analog of codex's stdin-hang) is the PERMISSION prompt — headless `run` blocks on an 'ask' permission, cleared via opencode.json `permission: allow` (0.15.3 has no --auto flag; newer builds add --auto/yolo). (C — the strategic win, essentially FREE) OpenCode is an MCP client: opencode.json `mcp` block takes `type:local` (stdio → our `hb mcp-serve`) or `type:remote` (url → `hb mcp-serve --http`); MCP tools auto-available to the model. Our dual-stack server already serves it (opencode 0.15.3 speaks the `initialize` handshake → our byte-identical old path), and the server is already proven spec-compliant against the official SDK v2 reference client. (B) OpenCode does NOT read `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (unlike Codex) — its extension model is `.opencode/` + `opencode.json`, so 'registering' HeartBeat is a documented `mcp` config snippet, not a marketplace plugin. Proof discipline (same as codex): a deterministic stub-`opencode`-on-PATH suite proof (no model/network) for the backend, a deterministic config-valid+server-runs proof for the MCP wiring, and an HONEST on-demand live tier (opencode+ollama needs the AI-SDK provider install and is best-effort — like codex's --oss). Both runtimes + registry for the backend (new shared surface → parity).

tasks.title: Author the stub-on-PATH backend proof
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/opencode-backend.sh mirroring codex-backend.sh — a stub `opencode` on PATH that emulates `opencode run` (parses the cwd/args, writes the artifact the gate checks, exits 0, reads/ignores stdin so it can't hang) drives the REAL opencode adapter via `HB_EXEC_BACKEND=opencode hb exec run` and the phase completes through its behavioral gate; a FAILING stub `opencode` (exits 1, writes nothing) does NOT complete the phase (the driver never fakes completion). Print OPENCODE-BACKEND-OK. Docker-free suite proof — no model, no network.

tasks.title: Python opencode backend
tasks.description: Add py/src/heartbeat/backends/opencode.py mirroring backends/codex.py: execute shells out to `opencode run --format json` in cwd with the prompt as the message arg, stdin CLOSED (defensive; opencode reads the prompt from argv), model via HB_EXEC_MODEL (and HB_EXEC_PROVIDER — e.g. `ollama/<model>` when provider=ollama) passed as `-m <model>`; ok = returncode==0, summary from stdout (JSON events / text); degrade to {ok:false}/{refuted:false} if `opencode` not on PATH. refute runs `opencode run` with a refuter prompt. Register `opencode` in backends/__init__ (_KNOWN and _MODULES). Do NOT try to manage opencode's permission config from the adapter — that is documented in the guide (headless autonomy needs opencode.json permission: allow on 0.15.3).

tasks.title: Plugin opencode executor + wiring
tasks.description: Add plugin/templates/executors/opencode-exec.sh mirroring claude-exec.sh/codex-exec.sh (same `opencode run --format json` invocation incl stdin closed and the model flag; degrade cleanly if opencode absent). Wire hb-exec.js defaultCmd `opencode`→opencode-exec.sh. Keep the registry/defaultCmd names matching the python side (parity of the shared backend surface).

tasks.title: Author the MCP-config proof
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/opencode-mcp.sh — a DETERMINISTIC proof (no opencode, no model, no network) that HeartBeat's documented opencode.json `mcp` config is valid AND runnable: build the canonical config object (mcp.heartbeat = {type:'local', command:['hb','mcp-serve'], enabled:true}, plus a remote variant {type:'remote', url}), assert it parses and has the opencode local-server shape (type/command), THEN spin the wired command (`hb mcp-serve`) as a subprocess and complete a JSON-RPC `initialize` handshake over stdio with our own client to confirm the exact command opencode would launch is a working MCP server. Also assert the guide documents an mcp config referencing `mcp-serve`. Print OPENCODE-MCP-OK. Note in-script that full-client interop is guaranteed by the official-SDK reference proof (tests/mcp-interop.sh) and the opencode-live check is on-demand.

tasks.title: Write the OpenCode guide + backend tables
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/use-heartbeat-with-opencode.md covering BOTH directions: (1) DRIVE opencode as Stage B — HB_EXEC_BACKEND=opencode; model/provider (`-m provider/model`; ollama for keyless-local); the permission/autonomy note (0.15.3 needs opencode.json `permission: allow` for headless, no --auto flag) and an HONEST live-tier note (opencode+ollama needs the AI-SDK provider install and is best-effort; the suite proof is the stub opencode-backend.sh). (2) BE DRIVEN by opencode over MCP — the opencode.json `mcp` snippet (type:local `hb mcp-serve`; type:remote `hb mcp-serve --http`), tools auto-available, link secure-the-mcp-server.md; note opencode uses its own config (not the .claude-plugin marketplace). Add `opencode` to the backend tables in dev-python.md / dev-plugin.md / heartbeat-py.md / choose-a-backend.md. Reference the real proofs (opencode-backend.sh, opencode-mcp.sh); only real commands.

tasks.title: Suite group + index
tasks.description: Add a Docker-free T72 group to tests/run-tests.sh: opencode-backend.sh (OPENCODE-BACKEND-OK), the registry resolves `opencode` in both runtimes (python get('opencode') + plugin defaultCmd/executor), opencode-mcp.sh (OPENCODE-MCP-OK), and prose-integrity on the guide (capture-to-file where a script emits multiple markers, to avoid the pipefail/SIGPIPE early-close). Index the guide in docs/howto/README.md and add a row to docs/howto/howto-list.md (E section) — and bump the 'mechanism guides' T-range header.

review.prompt: Refute that OB1 is done: does opencode-backend.sh drive the REAL opencode adapter (HB_EXEC_BACKEND=opencode) with the stub only standing in for the `opencode` CLI? Does the phase complete because the GATE passed (not because the stub said so), and is the failing-stub control load-bearing (phase does NOT complete)? Does the python adapter run `opencode run --format json` with the model flag and degrade to protocol-valid JSON without opencode? Do BOTH runtimes register `opencode` (registry + defaultCmd → opencode-exec.sh)? Is it a faithful mirror of the codex adapter? No model/network/Docker in the proof?
